notes: Expected to pass, up to step 13c: injection, both ledgers, netting, close, confirmation and settlement initiated on all three sides. "runUpTo": "13c" stops it once settlement has been initiated on all three sides (13, 13b, 13c), so steps 14, 15 and 15b (MT910 funding call and both settlement ledgers) are not run for it. No expect, so every step up to 13c must genuinely pass.
It is written as a one-entry trades list rather than a bare trade, because only a trades entry carries runUpTo and expect through to the runner.

The sheet states the trade as USD 55000 against CNH 370700. The netting rule is configured CNH-USD, in alphabetical order, so the pair is carried as CNHUSD with each amount on its own currency: 370700 CNH base, 55000 USD reference - the amounts TC017 carries for the same sheet values.
direction and Against list both options in the sheet. The first of each, Buy and Base, is used, matching the rest of the pack: BNKA-HK is the base currency buyer, partyDirection Buy.

The point of the row is the tenure: settlement is far in the future. {{T+800}} resolves to 800 calendar days after the run date, as the sheet's example states, so the date never goes stale; tradeDate is the run date. Steps 06 to 13c read the value date back from state, so netting, closing, confirmation and settlement initiation all use the T+800 date.
Steps 07 and 07b search for the trade's legs over a window that always includes its own value date, so a value date beyond the usual 30-day window is still found.
The T+800 date gets its own netting group, so the row does not share a group with the rows settling today on the same rule.

It nets under the BNKA-HK / BNKB-HK spot rule. That entry's mode in data/trade_scenarios.py decides steps 10, 11 and 11b: manual, as it is now, runs them to match the group's proposals; any other mode skips them and the group goes from closed to CONFIRMED by itself.

The sheet's expected processing - TS confirms the trade with pvpIntent true for both parties, Baton contracts 1 to 3 ACK, pre-registered then PVP: Accepted, no exceptions, TS notifies both parties - happens outside the APIs this suite calls, so it is recorded here only. What the suite checks is that the trade is accepted (04), booked on both ledgers (05, 05b), netted, confirmed and has settlement initiated on all three sides (13, 13b, 13c).
Event New and CRDS relation PVP are reference data in the sheet, recorded here only.
tradeReference, tradeReferenceSupplement and counterpartyReferenceNumber are free-text boxes, so they are generated per run as tradeId, the party partyTradeId and the counterparty partyTradeId.
ccpAlias, clearingBroker and counterpartyClearingBroker are blank in the sheet and have no wrapper field, so they are left out of the payload entirely.
Party CCP and Cpty CCP (both PVP) are legal-entity reference data in Baton, not trade fields, so they are recorded here and the payload carries the ordinary PVP settlement flag.
settlementCcy (USD) has no field in the wrapper, so it is recorded here only.
rate is carried as the sheet states it (2) even though 370700/55000 implies 6.74.
